t: The largest empire in West African history, Songhai controlled the Niger Bend and its trade cities of Gao, Timbuktu and Djenné.
Its wealth came from the trans-Saharan gold and salt trade, and its patronage made Timbuktu a centre of Islamic scholarship.
Weakened by civil war, it was shattered in 1591 by a small Moroccan army whose firearms routed a far larger Songhai force at Tondibi.
dyk: The traveller Leo Africanus, visiting Timbuktu around 1510, reported that books were sold there at greater profit than any other merchandise.
ev: Sunni Ali begins his reign and launches campaigns of conquest
Sunni Ali takes Timbuktu from the Tuareg
Djenné submits to Songhai after a long siege
Muhammad Ture defeats Sunni Baru and takes the title Askia
Askia Muhammad sets out on his pilgrimage to Mecca
Askia Muhammad is deposed by his son Askia Musa
Civil war divides the Songhai Empire
Judar Pasha's Moroccan army routs Askia Ishaq II at the Battle of Tondibi
